title: Error Budget Arbitration and Cross-Service Routing Runbook
author: Asha Kapoor
body:
Summary:
This runbook defines the procedures for arbitrating shared error budgets across multiple Redwood services, applying automated and manual traffic-routing policies, and documenting decisions during cross-service reliability events. It is intended for SREs, platform engineers, and service owners who operate multi-tenant or interdependent inference services (Hosted API, Dedicated routing, Private gateways).

Goals:
- Ensure predictable, auditable decisions when error budgets are scarce.
- Provide a clear sequence of automated mitigations and human arbitration steps.
- Minimize customer impact while preserving critical SLAs for prioritized workloads.

Scope:
- Applies to services that either: (a) share a physical pool (GPU cluster, region) or (b) are connected by request routing policies (fallbacks, canaries, model variants).
- Not intended for pure data-plane failures (network fabric outages) — those follow incident runbooks.

Owner / Roles:
- Primary owner: SRE Platform (oncall rotation: platform-sre@example.redwood)
- Service owners: owning team for each affected service
- Arbitration lead: senior SRE on duty (escalation step after 20 minutes if automated mitigations insufficient)
- Executive stakeholder: Product reliability lead (notify for >2 hour service degradation or repeated arbitration events)

Prerequisites / Telemetry to have available:
- Active SLO dashboards (per-service and pooled-resource level) with: availability, p95 latency, error rate
- Error budget ledger accessible in the Console and via API (ledger.redwood.internal/v1/error-budgets)
- Current routing policy manifests stored in git (infra/routing-policies/)
- Oncall Slack channel and incident channel templates ready: #sre-arbitration, #incident-<service>

Decision matrix (abbreviated):
1) If pooled error budget >20% remaining: allow standard autoscaling and routing fallbacks.
2) If pooled error budget between 5–20% remaining: apply automated conservative routing and inform arbitration lead.
3) If pooled error budget <5% remaining OR p95 latency >SLO x 2: trigger manual arbitration and progressive traffic reduction for least critical routes.

Priority tiers (for arbitration):
- Tier 0: AuthN/AuthZ, Billing, Control-plane (must be preserved when possible)
- Tier 1: Customer-facing inference endpoints with enterprise SLAs (Dedicated customers pinned to capacity)
- Tier 2: Public Hosted API free/low-tier routes, internal batch jobs, non-critical analytics

Automated mitigations (order of operations):
1) Throttle low-priority rate-limited keys by applying quota reduction policy (CLI example below).
2) Increase batching threshold for meeting non-latency-sensitive workloads using batching-flow controller.
3) Redirect traffic to quantized model variants for routes flagged as tolerant to quality tradeoffs.
4) Activate regional spillover: shift traffic from the hot region to healthy region(s) subject to data residency constraints.

CLI & API examples:
- Reduce quota for a key (example):
  $ redwoodctl quotas update --key k_abc123 --qps 10 --reason "arb throttle: pooled EB <10%"

- Apply routing override (gitops manifest snippet, YAML):
  # infra/routing-policies/overrides/arb-2026-02-10.yaml
  routeOverrides:
    - service: inference-public-v1
      action: reduce-weight
      weight: 20
      reason: "arb - preserve Tier 1 capacity"

Prometheus queries and alerts to drive arbitration:
- Pooled error budget remaining (percent):
  sum(service:eb_remaining_percent{pool="gpu-eu-west"}) by (pool)
- If pooled_eb_percent < 10% for 10m -> fire arbitration-tier-warning alert (Severity: P2)
- If pooled_eb_percent < 5% for 5m or p95_latency > 2 * SLO for 5m -> fire arbitration-required (Severity: P1)

Manual arbitration procedure (step-by-step):
1) Triage (0-10 minutes):
   - Acknowledge the alert in #sre-arbitration and create an incident stub (use /incident create).
   - Post initial private summary: affected pools, pooled EB %, top 3 impacted services, impact window estimate.
2) Gather (10-25 minutes):
   - Pull ledger entries for the last 24h for each service: (API: /v1/error-budgets/{service}/history)
   - Confirm if any enterprise Reserved Capacity blocks reductions (check Dedicated contracts dashboard).
   - List current routing overrides and canary rollouts that could be reverted.
3) Execute automated mitigations (25-40 minutes):
   - Apply the mitigations in the Automated mitigations section, smallest blast radius first.
   - Record each change in the incident notes (who, what, why, manifest commit hash).
4) Arbitration (40-90 minutes):
   - If mitigations insufficient, convene arbitration: service owners + arbitration lead + product SLA owner.
   - Use the Priority tiers table to evaluate candidate reductions.
   - Make a single explicit routing decision: e.g., reduce hosted-public weight by 40% and redirect to rate-limited queue.
   - Announce decision with timeline and rollback criteria.

Rollback and verification:
- Post-change verification window: 10 minutes for latency metrics, 30 minutes for error-rate stabilization.
- Rollback criteria (automated): if p95 increases > 20% after change or error budget consumption accelerates, revert manifest.
- Manual rollback: authorization required by arbitration lead and service owner. Document reason and time.

Post-event artifacts (what must be produced within 24 hours):
- Incident summary in Confluence (fill the Incident Evidence template). Include: timeline, decision log, manifest commits, cost impact estimate, and follow-ups.
- Update error-budget ledger with arbitration decisions (fields: decision_id, services_impacted, delta_eb_alloc, rationale).
- Open follow-up actions (Jira tickets) for remediation: capacity changes, SLA renegotiation, or automation improvements.

Example arbitration message (Slack template):
- Channel: #sre-arbitration
- Message:
  [ARBITRATION] Pool gpu-eu-west pooled_eb=3.2% -> reducing hosted-public weight by 35% to protect Tier1 Dedicated customers.
  Owner: @priya.menon, Action window: 40m, Rollback criteria: p95 > SLO * 1.2 after 10m.
  Commits: infra/routing-policies/overrides/arb-2026-02-10.yaml (sha: a1b2c3d)

Governance & auditability:
- All arbitration decisions must be accompanied by a git manifest commit and at least one Restore/Undo manifest created at the time of change.
- Arbitration events that result in customer-visible degradation require a post-incident review (PIR) within 3 business days.
- Repeated arbitrations (>3 in a 30-day rolling window) trigger a Reliability Initiative and capacity remediation plan owned by SRE Platform + affected service teams.

Automations to implement (roadmap items):
- Auto-suggest routing overrides based on historical quality sensitivity (Q-Score) per route.
- A command to generate rollback manifest automatically when applying an override.
- Better ledger UI: show per-service contribution to pooled consumption and projected time-to-exhaustion under current trends.

Appendix: Sample SLO / Error budget table (example for an inference service)
| Metric | SLO | Window | Error budget (tokens) | Alert threshold |
|--------|-----|--------|-----------------------|-----------------|
| Availability | 99.95% | 30d | 435 min downtime | EB<10% -> warn |
| p95 latency | 350ms | 30d | N/A | p95>700ms -> P1 |
| 5xx error rate | 0.5% | 30d | 135k errors | EB<5% -> arbitration |

Contacts and escalation links:
- Platform SRE Pager: +1-555-0110 (PagerDuty: platform-oncall)
- Arbitration Slack: #sre-arbitration
- Incident template: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/incident-template (use when creating the PIR)

Notes and rationale:
This runbook was authored to codify how we make tradeoffs when multiple services draw from shared capacity or pooled error budgets. The emphasis is on small blast-radius automation followed by rapid human arbitration with clear audit trails. The team should review this runbook quarterly and after any arbitration that required manual escalation.

References:
- Error budget ledger API docs: /internal/api/error-budgets
- Routing policy gitops README: infra/routing-policies/README.md
- SLO definitions and ownership: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/slo-catalog
